blocks.text: Yeh Unit 14 (Vectors in Space) ke poore unit se practice short questions (mukhtasar sawal) hain, unit ke sections ki tarteeb mein, Board ke 2 number wale sawal ke andaz mein. Har sawal mukhtasar qadmon mein hal kiya gaya hai.
14.1 Vectors (Recall)

blocks.prompt:
1 Define a scalar and a vector, with two examples of each.
(Scalar aur vector ki definition likhein, har aik ki do misalein dein.)
blocks.explanation: Scalar woh quantity hai jis ki sirf magnitude (miqdaar) ho, maslan mass aur temperature. Vector woh quantity hai jis ki magnitude aur direction (simt) dono hon, maslan displacement aur force.

book_ref.quote: A scalar is a quantity that has only magnitude or size

blocks.prompt:
2 When are two vectors parallel? Show that \([2, -3]\) and \([-6, 9]\) are parallel.
(Do vectors kab parallel hote hain? Dikhayein ke \([2, -3]\) aur \([-6, 9]\) parallel hain.)
blocks.explanation: Do vectors parallel hote hain agar aik doosre ka non-zero scalar multiple ho. Yahan \([-6, 9] = -3[2, -3]\), is liye parallel hain (ulti simt).

book_ref.quote: Two vectors are parallel if and only if they are non-zero scalar multiples of each other

blocks.text: 14.1.1 Rectangular Coordinate System in Space

blocks.prompt:
3 State the right-hand rule for labelling the axes of a rectangular coordinate system in space.
(Space ke rectangular coordinate system ke axes ke liye right-hand rule bayan karein.)
blocks.explanation: Right hand ki ungliyan positive x-axis ki taraf rakhein aur unhein positive y-axis ki taraf modein; angootha positive z-axis ki taraf hoga.

book_ref.quote: These axes are also labeled in accordance with the right-hand rule.

blocks.prompt:
4 Describe how the point \(P(3, -2, 5)\) is located in space.
(Point \(P(3, -2, 5)\) space mein kaise maloom kiya jata hai?)
blocks.explanation: Origin \(O\) se shuru karein; 3 unit positive x-axis par, phir 2 unit negative y-axis ke parallel, phir 5 unit oopar z-axis ke parallel. Tarteeb hamesha \(x\), \(y\), \(z\).

book_ref.quote: In space a rectangular coordinate system is constructed using three mutually orthogonal

blocks.text: 14.1.2 Concept of a Vector in Space

blocks.prompt:
5 What is \(R^{3}\)? How is a vector in space linked to a point of \(R^{3}\)?
(\(R^{3}\) kya hai? Space ka vector \(R^{3}\) ke point se kaise juda hai?)
blocks.explanation: \(R^{3} = \{(x, y, z) : x, y, z \in R\}\) 3-dimensional space hai. Har vector \(\underline{u}\) ke liye aik hi point \(P(x, y, z)\) hai jis ke liye \(\underline{OP} = \underline{u}\), is liye \(\underline{u} = [x, y, z]\).

book_ref.quote: is called 3-dimensional space

blocks.text: 14.1.3 Fundamental Mathematical Operations for Vectors in Space

blocks.prompt:
6 If \(\underline{u} = [1, 3, -2]\) and \(\underline{v} = [2, -1, 4]\), find \(2\underline{u} - 3\underline{v}\).
(Agar \(\underline{u} = [1, 3, -2]\) aur \(\underline{v} = [2, -1, 4]\) hon to \(2\underline{u} - 3\underline{v}\) nikalein.)

book_ref.quote: We define addition and scalar multiplication in

blocks.prompt:
8 For \(A(3, -1, 2)\) and \(B(1, 4, -3)\), find \(\underline{AB}\) and \(\underline{BA}\).
(\(A(3, -1, 2)\) aur \(B(1, 4, -3)\) ke liye \(\underline{AB}\) aur \(\underline{BA}\) nikalein.)

book_ref.quote: Such vectors are called position vectors in

blocks.text: 14.1.4 Magnitude of a Vector in Space

blocks.prompt:
9 Find the magnitude of \(\underline{u} = [3, -4, 12]\).
(\(\underline{u} = [3, -4, 12]\) ki magnitude nikalein.)

book_ref.quote: We define the magnitude, norm, or length of a vector

blocks.prompt:
10 If \(\underline{u} = [2, 1, -2]\) and \(\underline{v} = [1, 0, 3]\), find \(|\underline{u} - 2\underline{v}|\).
(Agar \(\underline{u} = [2, 1, -2]\) aur \(\underline{v} = [1, 0, 3]\) hon to \(|\underline{u} - 2\underline{v}|\) nikalein.)

book_ref.quote: We define the magnitude, norm, or length of a vector

blocks.text: 14.1.5 Components of a Vector

blocks.prompt:
11 Define a unit vector and find the unit vector in the direction of \(6\underline{i} - 2\underline{j} + 3\underline{k}\).
(Unit vector ki definition likhein aur \(6\underline{i} - 2\underline{j} + 3\underline{k}\) ki simt mein unit vector nikalein.)
blocks.explanation: Unit vector woh vector hai jis ki magnitude 1 ho. \(|\underline{u}| = 7\), is liye \(\hat{u} = \dfrac{1}{7}(6\underline{i} - 2\underline{j} + 3\underline{k})\).

book_ref.quote: A unit vector is defined as a vector whose magnitude is unity.

blocks.prompt:
12 Find a vector of magnitude 9 in the direction of \(2\underline{i} - \underline{j} + 2\underline{k}\).
(\(2\underline{i} - \underline{j} + 2\underline{k}\) ki simt mein 9 magnitude wala vector nikalein.)
blocks.explanation: Magnitude 3; unit vector ko 9 se zarb dein: \(6\underline{i} - 3\underline{j} + 6\underline{k}\).

book_ref.quote: A unit vector is defined as a vector whose magnitude is unity.

blocks.prompt:
13 Show that \(4\underline{i} - 6\underline{j} + 2\underline{k}\) and \(-6\underline{i} + 9\underline{j} - 3\underline{k}\) are parallel.
(Dikhayein ke \(4\underline{i} - 6\underline{j} + 2\underline{k}\) aur \(-6\underline{i} + 9\underline{j} - 3\underline{k}\) parallel hain.)
blocks.explanation: Doosra vector pehle ka \(-\frac{3}{2}\) guna hai, is liye parallel (ulti simt).

book_ref.quote: can be uniquely represented by

blocks.text: 14.1.6 Properties of Vectors

blocks.prompt:
14 Prove that \(a(b\underline{u}) = (ab)\underline{u}\) for \(\underline{u} = [x, y, z]\) and \(a, b \in R\).
(Saabit karein ke \(\underline{u} = [x, y, z]\) aur \(a, b \in R\) ke liye \(a(b\underline{u}) = (ab)\underline{u}\).)
blocks.explanation: \(a(b\underline{u}) = a[bx, by, bz] = [(ab)x, (ab)y, (ab)z] = (ab)\underline{u}\); real numbers ka qanoon \(a(bx) = (ab)x\) har component mein lagaya.

book_ref.quote: The proofs of the other parts are left as an exercise for the students.

blocks.prompt:
15 What are the additive identity and the additive inverse of \(\underline{u} = [x, y, z]\) in \(R^{3}\)?
(\(R^{3}\) mein \(\underline{u} = [x, y, z]\) ki additive identity aur additive inverse kya hain?)

book_ref.quote: is the additive inverse of \(\underline{u}\)

blocks.text: 14.1.7 Distance Between Two Points in Space

blocks.prompt:
16 Find the distance between \(P_{1}(-1, 2, 5)\) and \(P_{2}(3, -2, 3)\).
(\(P_{1}(-1, 2, 5)\) aur \(P_{2}(3, -2, 3)\) ka faasla nikalein.)

book_ref.quote: This is called distance formula between two points

blocks.prompt:
17 Find \(k\) if the distance between \((k, 1, 2)\) and \((1, 3, 4)\) is 3.
(\(k\) nikalein agar \((k, 1, 2)\) aur \((1, 3, 4)\) ka faasla 3 ho.)

book_ref.quote: This is called distance formula between two points

blocks.text: 14.1.8 Direction Angles and Direction Cosines of a Vector

blocks.prompt:
18 Find the direction cosines of \(\underline{r} = 2\underline{i} - 3\underline{j} + 6\underline{k}\).
(\(\underline{r} = 2\underline{i} - 3\underline{j} + 6\underline{k}\) ke direction cosines nikalein.)

book_ref.quote: are called direction cosines of the vector

blocks.prompt:
19 Can \(120^{\circ}, 45^{\circ}, 60^{\circ}\) be the direction angles of a vector?
(Kya \(120^{\circ}, 45^{\circ}, 60^{\circ}\) kisi vector ke direction angles ho sakte hain?)
blocks.explanation: \(\frac{1}{4} + \frac{1}{2} + \frac{1}{4} = 1\): shart poori hai, is liye haan.

book_ref.quote: The angles \(\alpha\), \(\beta\) and \(\gamma\) are called the direction angles.

blocks.prompt:
20 Prove that \(\cos^{2}\alpha + \cos^{2}\beta + \cos^{2}\gamma = 1\) for the direction angles of \(\underline{r} = x\underline{i} + y\underline{j} + z\underline{k}\).
(\(\underline{r} = x\underline{i} + y\underline{j} + z\underline{k}\) ke direction angles ke liye saabit karein: \(\cos^{2}\alpha + \cos^{2}\beta + \cos^{2}\gamma = 1\).)

book_ref.quote: Prove that \(\cos^{2}\alpha + \cos^{2}\beta + \cos^{2}\gamma = 1\).

blocks.prompt:
21 A vector makes \(\alpha = 45^{\circ}\) and \(\beta = 60^{\circ}\) with \(\underline{i}\) and \(\underline{j}\), and \(\gamma\) is obtuse. Find \(\gamma\).
(Aik vector \(\underline{i}\), \(\underline{j}\) ke saath \(\alpha = 45^{\circ}\), \(\beta = 60^{\circ}\) banata hai aur \(\gamma\) obtuse hai. \(\gamma\) nikalein.)

book_ref.quote: are called direction cosines of the vector

blocks.text: 14.2.1 Dot or Scalar Product of Two Vectors and Its Geometrical Interpretation

blocks.prompt:

(Do non-zero vectors ke dot (scalar) product ki definition likhein.)
blocks.explanation: Aik hi initial point wale non-zero vectors ke liye \(\underline{u} \cdot \underline{v} = |\underline{u}||\underline{v}|\cos\theta\), jahan \(\theta\) darmiyani angle hai, \(0 \le \theta \le \pi\). Jawab scalar hai.

book_ref.quote: The dot product of \(\underline{u}\) and \(\underline{v}\), written as

blocks.prompt:
23 If \(|\underline{u}| = 2\), \(|\underline{v}| = 3\) and \(\underline{u} \cdot \underline{v} = 3\), find the angle between \(\underline{u}\) and \(\underline{v}\).
(Agar \(|\underline{u}| = 2\), \(|\underline{v}| = 3\) aur \(\underline{u} \cdot \underline{v} = 3\) ho to darmiyani angle nikalein.)

book_ref.quote: The dot product of \(\underline{u}\) and \(\underline{v}\), written as

blocks.text: 14.2.2 Deduction of the Important Results

blocks.prompt:
24 Using \(\underline{i} \cdot \underline{i} = 1\) and \(\underline{i} \cdot \underline{j} = 0\) (and similar results), evaluate \((\underline{i} + 2\underline{j} - \underline{k}) \cdot (3\underline{i} - \underline{j})\).
(\(\underline{i} \cdot \underline{i} = 1\), \(\underline{i} \cdot \underline{j} = 0\) waghera se \((\underline{i} + 2\underline{j} - \underline{k}) \cdot (3\underline{i} - \underline{j})\) nikalein.)

book_ref.quote: By applying the definition of dot product to unit vectors

blocks.text: 14.2.3 Projection of a Vector along Another Vector

blocks.prompt:

(\(\underline{a} = 3\underline{i} + 4\underline{k}\) ka \(\underline{b} = 2\underline{i} + \underline{j} - 2\underline{k}\) ke saath projection, aur \(\underline{b}\) ka \(\underline{a}\) ke saath projection nikalein.)

book_ref.quote: Then \(\overline{OM}\) is called the projection of

blocks.prompt:
26 Give the geometrical meaning of the dot product.
(Dot product ka geometrical matlab bayan karein.)
blocks.explanation: \(\underline{u} \cdot \underline{v} = |\underline{u}|(|\underline{v}|\cos\theta)\): aik vector ki magnitude zarb doosre ka us par projection; yani aik vector doosre ki simt mein kitna phaila hai.

book_ref.quote: Thus, geometrically, the dot product of two vectors represents the product of the magnitude of one vector

blocks.text: 14.2.4 Properties of Dot Product

blocks.prompt:

(Agar \(|\underline{u}| = 3\), \(|\underline{v}| = 4\) aur \(\underline{u} \cdot \underline{v} = 2\) ho to \(|\underline{u} + \underline{v}|\) nikalein.)

book_ref.quote: be vectors and let \(c\) be any real number, then

blocks.text: 14.2.5 Dot Product of Vectors in terms of their components

blocks.prompt:
28 Find \(\underline{u} \cdot \underline{v}\) for \(\underline{u} = 4\underline{i} - \underline{j} + 2\underline{k}\) and \(\underline{v} = -\underline{i} + 3\underline{j} + 5\underline{k}\).
(\(\underline{u} = 4\underline{i} - \underline{j} + 2\underline{k}\) aur \(\underline{v} = -\underline{i} + 3\underline{j} + 5\underline{k}\) ka dot product nikalein.)

book_ref.quote: Hence the dot product of two vectors is the sum of the product of their corresponding components.

blocks.text: 14.2.6 Orthogonality of Two Vectors

blocks.prompt:

(Dikhayein ke \(3\underline{i} - 2\underline{j} + \underline{k}\) aur \(2\underline{i} + 5\underline{j} + 4\underline{k}\) orthogonal hain.)
blocks.explanation: Dot product \(6 - 10 + 4 = 0\); dono non-zero hain, is liye perpendicular.

book_ref.quote: are perpendicular if and only if

blocks.prompt:

(\(\alpha\) nikalein taake \(\alpha\underline{i} + 2\underline{j} + \alpha\underline{k}\) aur \(3\underline{i} - \underline{j} + \underline{k}\) perpendicular hon.)

book_ref.quote: are perpendicular if and only if

blocks.text: 14.2.7 Angle Between Two Vectors

blocks.prompt:

(\(\underline{u} = \underline{i} - \underline{j}\) aur \(\underline{v} = \underline{j} - \underline{k}\) ka darmiyani angle nikalein.)

book_ref.quote: The angle between two vectors \(\underline{u}\) and \(\underline{v}\) is determined from the definition of dot product

blocks.text: 14.2.8 Work done By a Constant Force

blocks.prompt:

(Constant force ke work done ki definition likhein aur isay dot product ki shakal mein likhein.)
blocks.explanation: Work done = displacement ki simt mein \(\underline{F}\) ka component zarb faasla: \(W = (F\cos\theta)(AB) = \underline{F} \cdot \underline{d}\).

book_ref.quote: the work done by \(\underline{F}\) is defined to be the product of the component of

blocks.text: 14.3.1 The Cross Product or Vector Product of Two Vectors and its Geometrical Interpretation

blocks.prompt:
34 Define the cross (vector) product of two non-zero vectors.
(Do non-zero vectors ke cross (vector) product ki definition likhein.)
blocks.explanation: \(\underline{u} \times \underline{v} = (|\underline{u}||\underline{v}|\sin\theta)\underline{n}\); \(\theta\) darmiyani angle (\(0 \le \theta \le \pi\)) aur \(\underline{n}\) dono ke plane par amood unit vector hai jis ki simt right-hand rule deta hai.

blocks.prompt:

(\(\underline{u} \times \underline{v}\) ki simt kaise maloom hoti hai?)
blocks.explanation: Right-hand rule se: ungliyan \(\underline{u}\) ki taraf rakh kar \(\underline{v}\) ki taraf modein; angootha \(\underline{u} \times \underline{v}\) ki simt batata hai.

book_ref.quote: then curl towards the vector

(\((\underline{i} \times \underline{j}) \times \underline{i}\) aur \(\underline{i} \times (\underline{j} \times \underline{i})\) nikalein.)

book_ref.quote: By applying the definition of cross product to unit vectors

blocks.prompt:

(Definition se dikhayein ke \(\underline{u} \times \underline{u} = \underline{0}\).)
blocks.explanation: \(\underline{u}\) ka apne aap se angle 0 hai, \(\sin 0 = 0\), is liye \(\underline{u} \times \underline{u} = \underline{0}\).

blocks.text: 14.4.5 Coplanar Vectors and Condition for Coplanarity of Three Vectors

blocks.prompt:

(Dikhayein ke \(\underline{u} \cdot (\underline{u} \times \underline{v}) = 0\).)
blocks.explanation: Yeh \([\underline{u}\ \underline{u}\ \underline{v}]\) hai jis mein do vectors barabar hain, is liye zero; \(\underline{u} \times \underline{v}\) to \(\underline{u}\) par amood hai.
